source_policy: Curated paths through existing published online readings; no new philosophical claims or altered source texts

paths.title: Begin with the ideas
paths.prompt: I'm curious, but I'm new to this philosophy.
paths.description: Meet the central ideas before choosing a longer book.
paths.reflection: Which idea interests you most, and which one would you want to question?

steps.title: An invitation, not an entrance exam
steps.source: A Beginner's Guide to Confluent Humanism
steps.why: Start with an invitation to explore without agreeing to everything.

steps.title: Arrival
steps.why: Consider how beginnings and conditions we did not choose shape our possibilities.

steps.title: A compass, not a scorecard
steps.why: Meet Hope, Acceptance, Reflection, Growth and Community as complementary values.

paths.title: Uncertainty and hope
paths.prompt: I want to think about a future I cannot predict.
paths.description: Explore possibility without turning hope into a guarantee.
paths.reflection: What is still uncertain here, and what is one thing you can realistically influence?

steps.title: The Open Future
steps.why: Explore the difference between the unknown and what may not yet be settled.

steps.title: Hope
steps.why: Consider hope alongside present limits, grief and the need for support.

steps.title: A Hope Without a Guarantee
steps.why: Test what responsible encouragement could look like in an uncertain situation.

paths.title: Fairness and circumstance
paths.prompt: I'm thinking about why people start from different places.
paths.description: Look at unequal conditions without reducing anyone to their circumstances.
paths.reflection: When have I mistaken an available option for an opportunity everyone could actually use?

steps.title: Arrival
steps.why: Notice what we inherit before our first choices.

steps.title: The Weight of a Starting Place
steps.source: The Little Book of Possibilities · Chapter 3
steps.why: Ask whether an opportunity is genuinely accessible, not just formally offered.

steps.title: Two Flood Marks
steps.why: Follow a fictional community facing different losses after the same event.

paths.title: Choices and consequences
paths.prompt: I want to think about responsibility when outcomes go wrong.
paths.description: Separate a sound decision from the result that follows it.
paths.reflection: How could I assess a decision using what was reasonably knowable at the time?

steps.title: Action Within Uncertainty
steps.why: Consider meaningful action within limits and responsibilities.

steps.title: When Good Choices Lead to Bad Outcomes
steps.why: Examine why a difficult result does not automatically prove a careless decision.

steps.title: When Good Choices Fail
steps.why: Compare hindsight, accountability and fairness in an imagined scenario.

paths.title: Learning and growth
paths.prompt: I'm interested in changing, learning or trying something new.
paths.description: Treat growth as developing capacities, not proving personal worth.
paths.reflection: What would help make a small learning opportunity accessible and sustainable?

steps.title: Growth
steps.why: Explore personal, intellectual, emotional and social development.

steps.title: Learning Without a Ladder
steps.source: The Little Book of Possibilities · Chapter 8
steps.why: Consider reciprocal learning without ranking people by expertise or status.

steps.title: Reflection and Growth
steps.why: Notice what experience may teach without treating every setback as personal failure.

paths.title: Connection and generosity
paths.prompt: I'm interested in how people can help one another.
paths.description: Consider the value—and the boundaries—of sharing good fortune.
paths.reflection: What kind of help could I offer or request without creating an unwanted obligation?

steps.title: Shared Fortune
steps.why: Consider what knowledge, safety, time or connection might make possible.

steps.title: What Do We Owe to Strangers?
steps.why: Explore the scope and limits of responsibility to people we have not met.

steps.title: A Place Without a Price
steps.why: Discuss dignity, access and what membership should not demand.

paths.title: The wider living world
paths.prompt: I'm curious about our responsibilities beyond other people.
paths.description: Reflect on living systems and the effects of human choices.
paths.reflection: Whose interests—including non-human lives—might be missing from a decision?

steps.title: The Living World
steps.why: Explore why the living world matters beyond its immediate usefulness to us.

steps.title: Beyond the Human Circle
steps.why: Consider how human needs and ecological responsibilities can come into tension.

steps.title: The Path Through the Reeds
steps.why: Encounter a fictional decision involving a shared path and an ecosystem.

paths.title: Belief and the unknown
paths.prompt: I have questions about religion, evidence or what follows life.
paths.description: Make room for conviction, uncertainty and respectful disagreement.
paths.reflection: Which of my beliefs are personal convictions, and which are claims I would want evidence to test?

steps.title: Is the Fellowship of Chance a religion?
steps.why: Begin with a straightforward explanation of the proposed community's identity.

steps.title: Is this a religion, a philosophy or a community?
steps.why: Explore what agreement and participation do—and do not—require.

steps.title: Death and the Unknown
steps.why: Consider mortality and uncertainty without requiring a shared answer.
